title: The unshifted nonnegative Wick Hamiltonians escape every finite spectral window

resolvent_collapse.ground_energy: For fixed g>0 let E_N=inf spec(H_N), where H_N is K1466's operator for q0+g W_N. K1474 gives E_N=Omega(log N)
resolvent_collapse.resolvent_bound: For every lambda>0, ||(H_N+lambda)^(-1)||=1/(E_N+lambda), hence the resolvents converge to zero in operator norm
resolvent_collapse.finite_limit_exclusion: The zero operator cannot be the resolvent of a densely defined self-adjoint operator. Therefore the unshifted family has no finite self-adjoint strong-resolvent limit; it converges only to the generalized infinite operator
resolvent_collapse.semibounded_recentering: For K_N=H_N-a_N, a uniformly lower-bounded nontrivial norm-resolvent or semibounded Mosco limit requires E_N-a_N=O(1); equivalently the scalar counterterm must track the true interacting ground energy up to bounded error
resolvent_collapse.martingale_shift_boundary: The exact projective shift 6g C_N^2 is not known to track E_N. Establishing E_N-6g C_N^2=O(1), or selecting another a_N with recovery-sequence compactness, is a new theorem rather than a consequence of Wick martingality
resolvent_collapse.ceiling: This decides the unshifted nonnegative family only. It neither computes E_N sharply nor excludes a ground-energy-recentered limit, non-Gaussian reference measure, singular dressing or changed representation
